## Research question and network

::::: columns
::: {.column width="38%"}
**How might JRL and CRL change destination choice and access to stations?**

184 existing physical stations.

The brief's 24 JRL and 12 CRL Phase 1 line stations add **29 sites** and upgrade **7 interchanges**.

The expanded choice set has **213 destinations**.

Origins remain the existing boarding stations. The scenario redistributes their recorded trips.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-study
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.6
th3_plot_study(res)
```
:::
:::::

::: notes
Source: LTA DataMall and the station coordinate repository linked in the assignment. The report records the pinned repository revision and the station reconciliation. The core scope excludes Forest Hill and later CRL phases. An interchange upgrade is not a new duplicate station. https://isss626-ay2026-27aug.netlify.app/take-home_ex03
:::

## Observed travel pattern

```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-observed
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.7
th3_plot_observed(res)
```

**Data:** LTA train OD, August to October 2026. Models use weekday destination arrivals, not daily averages or transfer volumes.

Station demand varies widely. The monthly departure profiles give context for using weekdays as one consistent target.

::: notes
Source: the project's six LTA ridership snapshots and exact quality checks. The three OD files contain 2,704,578 raw rows. Separate tap in and tap out data do not reconcile exactly with OD totals, so every model target and origin total comes from the OD source. https://datamall.lta.gov.sg/content/datamall/en/dynamic-data.html
:::

## Analytical approach

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Course methods**

-   Chapter 15: prepare station OD tables.
-   Chapter 16: origin constrained Poisson `glm()`.
-   Chapter 18: Huff and MCI choice probabilities.

$$\widehat T_{ij}=M_i\frac{\exp(\beta X_{ij})}{\sum_{k\ne i}\exp(\beta X_{ik})}$$

Predictors: straight line distance, bus stops within 800 m, line count, HDB footprint and LRT status.
:::

::: {.column width="47%"}
**Evaluation design**

| Period    | Role                        |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| August    | Fit coefficients            |
| September | Select the structural model |
| October   | Evaluate fixed coefficients |

The baseline and future scenarios share October origin totals.

**Additional analysis:** nearest station accessibility, assumption sensitivity and spatial residual checks.
:::
:::::

::: notes
Origin totals are supplied for each evaluation month, so the test measures conditional allocation rather than forecasting unknown network demand. The alternative historical OD benchmark has no observations for unopened destinations. https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap16.html https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap18.html
:::

## Model validation

```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-validation
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.7
th3_plot_validation(res)
```

The selected MCI model has **`r pct(score$station_WAPE)` station WAPE** in October. Historical shares perform much better for existing stations, but cannot directly predict new sites.

The future estimates need cautious interpretation. They omit employment, actual rail travel time and service frequency.

::: notes
Source: model_validation.csv and october_station_predictions.csv, generated from the frozen LTA data. WAPE sums absolute station errors and divides by total observed arrivals. The line in the scatterplot marks equality. September selects MCI by OD log loss without using October to tune coefficients.
:::

## Future network scenario

```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-scenario
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.6
th3_plot_scenario(res)
```

New sites receive **`r pct(sum(scenario$future[scenario$new_site]) / sum(scenario$future))` of fixed demand**, about **`r sprintf("%.2f", sum(scenario$future[scenario$new_site]) / 1e6)` million** monthly weekday arrivals.

Both networks allocate the same **`r sprintf("%.2f", sum(scenario$future) / 1e6)` million** trips. These estimates exclude additional demand from new homes or new origins.

::: notes
Source: future_station_scenario.csv. Baseline and future use identical October origin totals and fitted August coefficients. The seven existing interchanges gain one rail line. The first two maps share the same size scale. Changes compare model against model, not against observed baseline arrivals.
:::

## Changes at individual stations

```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-impacts
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.9
th3_plot_impacts(res)
```

Hougang gains about **420,000** monthly arrivals in this specification. Outram Park loses about **214,000**. Serangoon North receives the largest new site allocation.

Interchange gains depend strongly on the fitted line count effect. They do not measure transfer load or crowding.

::: notes
Exact values come from future_station_scenario.csv. The scenario keeps current bus stop and HDB attributes. Line count is associated with arrivals in the observed data, but the analysis does not establish a causal effect of adding a new line.
:::

## Existing station markets

```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-markets
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.6
th3_plot_focus(res)
```

The most likely destination changes at **`r sum(e$market$changed)` of 184 origins**. The maps show Outram Park's allocation from each existing origin before and after expansion.

Huff and MCI redistribute shares through the choice denominator. They keep relative odds between unchanged destinations, which limits the representation of changed routes and transfers.

::: notes
Source: the complete eligible OD choice matrices and origin_market_changes.csv. These are discrete station origin markets, not residential walking catchments. The black star identifies the destination. The probability scales match across the first two panels.
:::

## Added analysis: geographic access

```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-access
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.5
th3_plot_access(res)
```

**`r fmt(coverage$newly_covered)` HDB building records** become newly within 800 m. Coverage rises from **`r pct(coverage$baseline / coverage$total_buildings)` to `r pct(coverage$expanded / coverage$total_buildings)`**. The west accounts for **731** newly covered records.

**Pasir Ris East** leads in newly covered buildings (219), while **Serangoon North** leads the arrival allocation. Demand and access rankings answer different planning questions.

::: caption
Straight line distances to station points. Building counts include nonresidential HDB structures.
:::

::: notes
Source: HDB Existing Building snapshot, the same existing and proposed station coordinates, and accessibility_thresholds.csv. Method follows the nearest facility and threshold accessibility ideas in Chapter 17. Distances are straight lines in EPSG:3414. Counts include nonresidential HDB structures and cannot be interpreted as people, households or verified walking access. https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap17.html https://data.gov.sg/datasets/d_16b157c52ed637edd6ba1232e026258d/view
:::

## Assumption sensitivity

```{r}
#| label: th3-slide-sensitivity
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.7
th3_plot_sensitivity(res)
```

The five MCI cases assign **5.9% to 15.5%** of fixed demand to new sites. The top ranked new site changes. These ranges are stress tests, not confidence intervals.

Calibrated Huff predicts aggregate interchange losses, while MCI predicts gains. The sign depends on whether attraction includes line count.

::: notes
Source: scenario_sensitivity.csv and new_station_sensitivity_ranges.csv. The MCI cases change distance decay by 25% or new site attraction to 0.5 or 1.5 times the baseline score, one assumption at a time. The access result remains positive at 500, 800 and 1,000 m thresholds, independent of the ridership model.
:::

## Planning and public safety

::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Evidence for follow up**

-   Pasir Ris East and western sites merit checks on crossings, entrances and step free routes because of their access gains.
-   Hougang and Ang Mo Kio merit detailed interchange flow checks under the MCI scenario.
-   Both passenger allocation and local access matter when comparing sites.

**The study does not establish a reduction in accidents or crowding.**
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Limits that affect decisions**

-   October error remains high. Residual Moran's I is about 0.11 to 0.13 across tested neighbours, indicating spatially patterned error.
-   Monthly arrivals cannot reveal peak occupancy or platform capacity.
-   New housing, new origins, walking routes and future operating plans need additional data.

[Full results and assumptions](take-home_ex03.qmd)
:::
:::::

::: notes
Source: residual_moran.csv, future_station_scenario.csv and the accessibility comparison. Symmetric nearest neighbour weights, k=6,8,10, row standardisation and 999 permutations yield p=0.001 in each exploratory check. These diagnostics are not an independent validation set. Public safety recommendations are proposals for further assessment, not evidence of safety outcomes. AI assisted code organisation and drafting. The author should review the analysis and conclusions before submission.
:::
